hipaa-check 1.1.2

- Added automatic anonymous trial mode: new users can now run up to 5 scored HIPAA checks with a local anon ID and no registration.
- Seamless trial-to-account transfer: registering after using the trial preserves progress and upgrades to a full free API Key (100 calls).
- The skill now auto-launches the 5-run trial without requiring any API Key; registration is prompted only after the trial ends.
- Updated usage instructions and agent guide to include anonymous trial functionality.
- No changes to check items, scoring logic, or cloud destinations.

- Removed the skill-card.md file.
- No changes to functionality or features.
- Documentation and usage remain unchanged.

- Removed terminal-based account creation and login; free API Key must now be registered on the compliancehub.cn website.
- Guidance for API Key provisioning updated—no email/password entry in the terminal; obtain and supply the Key via environment variable or config file.
- Removed all references to the --login and --auth commands.
- Clarified security and data handling: account and credential submission handled only through the official website.
- Removed skill-card.md file.

- Updated --non-interactive preview mode to fetch the latest check items from the cloud rule library, falling back to the bundled set if the network is unavailable.
- Clarified that the free preview does not transmit user answers and only fetches items.
- Updated documentation to reflect changes in data flow and preview behavior.
- Removed redundant documentation file (skill-card.md).

Initial release — Free HIPAA Privacy/Security/Breach compliance check (cloud-scored, 12 items):

- Run a professional HIPAA compliance check covering 12 core criteria: Privacy, Security & Breach Notification Rules.
- Free to install and use; scoring runs on the CQDev cloud via compliancehub.cn (100 free API calls after signup).
- Provides both a totally offline checklist preview and a full cloud-scored audit with downloadable report.
- Simple setup: get your API Key in seconds; keys are securely stored outside the skill folder.
- Security-focused: no shell execution, no external binaries, and transparent network handling.
- Clear agent instructions and usage examples for both interactive and non-interactive modes.
